**Goal:** independently navigate and maintain your own permitted workspace from a terminal. Use a test directory in your home folder rather than deleting or changing system files.

## Essential commands

| Task | Command | What to notice |
|---|---|---|
| Current location | `pwd` | Absolute path |
| List files | `ls -la` | Names, hidden files, permissions |
| Navigate | `cd`, `cd ..`, `cd ~` | Relative and home paths |
| Create workspace | `mkdir -p ~/tej-practice` | A safe folder for experiments |
| Create/edit text | `nano ~/tej-practice/notes.txt` | Save with Ctrl+O |
| Read text | `cat ~/tej-practice/notes.txt` | Content vs filename |
| Copy or move | `cp`, `mv` | Source and destination |
| Inspect help | `man ls`, `ls --help` | Read documentation |
| Inspect system | `uname -a`, `lscpu`, `free -h`, `df -h` | Kernel, CPU, RAM, free disk |
| Running processes | `top` or `htop` | Live CPU and memory use |

Use tab completion and command history. Explain the difference between `/`, `~` and `.`. Know what `sudo` does but do not run system-changing commands without teacher approval.

## 15-minute challenge

Create `~/tej-practice`, open a text file, record three commands you used and their purposes, copy the file to a backup name, then locate both files using the terminal. Demonstrate the result to a partner.

## Approved software setup

On Debian/Ubuntu/Mint systems, use the teacher's package list. `sudo apt update` refreshes package information; `sudo apt install <package>` installs a package, but the specific package and authorization must be known. Do not paste unknown Internet install scripts into a terminal.

## Evidence

Take a screenshot or record a few important commands and results. Explain one error message you encountered.
